title: An Agent's realized identity is readable from the Global Activation Status of each Primitive it holds
content:
Every Primitive Hub Document carries a one-word **Global Activation Status**. Across Pattern's Primitives the values differ meaningfully: Agent Creation is `Completed` (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.1.1), Prime Transformation is `Completed` (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.2.1.1), Executor Transformation is `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.3.1.1), the Agent Token Primitive is `Active` (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.4.1.1), and the Executor Accord Primitive is `Active` (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.1.1).

Read together, those five words are a complete profile of what the Agent actually is: it was created, it took the Prime transformation path and not the Executor one, it has a live token, and it is operationally engaged through an Accord. Consistently with `Inactive` Executor Transformation, A.6.1.1.6.2.1.2.3.1.1.1 declares "Pattern is a Prime Agent."

The pattern is that Sky does not store an Agent "type" field as the source of truth; type is a *consequence* of which transformation Primitives were Invoked. `Completed` versus `Active` also carries information: `Completed` marks the one-shot Genesis acts that are finished forever, while `Active` marks Primitives with live instances still under management.

The practical benefit is that a reader can audit an Agent's capabilities without trusting a summary — each claimed capability has a Primitive whose status either supports it or does not.
description: Pattern shows Agent Creation and Prime Transformation as Completed, Agent Token and Executor Accord as Active, and Executor Transformation as Inactive — a Prime Agent that never became an Executor.
